items.summary: A complete, free platform adventure: guide Tux through the classic Milestone 1 levels.
items.models: Native Vita; exact firmware range and PS TV support not specified by author.
items.prerequisites: Homebrew access and VitaShell. Game assets are bundled.
setup: Copy SuperTux-PSVITA.vpk to ux0:downloads/ and install with VitaShell.
Open the SuperTux bubble from LiveArea. Saves and settings use ux0:data/supertux/.

items.summary: A fast multiplayer rabbit arena with local controller and Bluetooth keyboard support.
items.models: Native Vita; no exact firmware minimum published. Multiplayer only.
items.prerequisites: Homebrew access, VitaShell and another player. Up to four players are supported by the port.
setup: Install jumpnbump_1.00.vpk with VitaShell; all required game data is included.
Prepare multiplayer input, then open its LiveArea bubble. Move with the D-pad or stick and jump with an action button.
The Vita build is 1.00. Release tag 1.02 contains later Switch changes; it is not Vita version 1.02.

items.summary: Marble puzzles built around matching hidden Oxyd stones, with mazes, traps and touch controls.
items.models: Native Vita; no exact firmware minimum or model restriction published.
items.prerequisites: Homebrew access, VitaShell and the matching free data ZIP.
setup: Install enigma_1.11.vpk with VitaShell.
Extract this project's data.zip into ux0:data/, retaining the enigma folder. Do not use Chocolate Doom's different data.zip.
The author recommends FTP when transferring the many small data files. Vita remains 1.11; release 1.16 updates Switch only.

items.summary: One native launcher for classic Doom, Heretic, Hexen and Strife engines, with shareware data available.
items.models: Native Vita; no exact firmware range or model restriction published.
items.prerequisites: Homebrew access, VitaShell and release data.zip. Full games need your own IWADs.
items.data: Shareware included; full-game data supplied by you
setup: Install ChocolateDoom_r3_1.vpk. The author marks Vita Release 3.1 as a pre-release.
Extract its data.zip at ux0: so the data/chocolate folder lands at ux0:data/chocolate/. This includes Doom and Heretic shareware.
Copy your own full-game IWADs to ux0:data/chocolate/iwads/. Put PWADs in the appropriate doom, heretic, hexen or strife subfolder under pwads/.

items.summary: The official native Vita emulator for Game Boy, Game Boy Color and Game Boy Advance.
items.models: Official Vita homebrew build; no exact firmware minimum or handheld model restriction published.
items.prerequisites: Homebrew access, VitaShell and your own game backups. External BIOS is optional.
items.data: Emulator only · bring your own games
setup: Install the ready VPK extracted unchanged from the official Vita 7z, or unpack the original archive on your computer.
Copy your own GB/GBC/GBA backups to a folder you choose, for example ux0:roms/gba/, then select them in mGBA's file browser.
The suggested ROM folder is for organization; upstream does not require that exact location.

items.summary: Native Nintendo 64 emulation with vitaGL rendering and a per-game compatibility database.
items.models: Author explicitly targets Vita / PS TV. Performance and compatibility vary by game.
items.prerequisites: Homebrew access, VitaShell, matching data ZIP and libshacccg.suprx for the renderer. Bring your own ROMs.
items.data: Emulator only · bring your own games
setup: Install DaedalusX64.vpk. Extract the matching ZIP into ux0:data/; its top-level DaedalusX64 folder must become ux0:data/DaedalusX64/.
Confirm libshacccg.suprx exists at ur0:data/libshacccg.suprx or ur0:data/external/libshacccg.suprx. This shader compiler is required by the pinned native build and is not bundled here.
Put your own N64 ROMs in ux0:data/DaedalusX64/Roms/. Check the compatibility list for each game.
The upstream Nightly identifies build 2026-10-12, commit fb7238e. These files preserve the snapshot retrieved on 2 November 2026, with individual SHA-256 hashes.

items.summary: Stream games from your own PC to Vita with touch controls, host pairing and Wake-on-LAN support.
items.models: Native Vita client. No exact firmware minimum published; touch features depend on handheld hardware.
items.prerequisites: Homebrew access, unsafe homebrew permission, Wi-Fi/LAN and a compatible Sunshine host on your PC.
items.data: PC host required · no PC games included
setup: Install moonlight.vpk with VitaShell. This build uses SceShell permission for optional PS-button capture.
Set up Sunshine on your PC, connect both devices to your local network, add the host in Moonlight and approve its pairing PIN on the PC.
Select a host app to stream. START + L + R opens the pause menu; START + LEFT opens the floating keyboard.

items.summary: Browse, install and customize Vita themes, then restyle app bubbles and LiveArea artwork.
items.models: HENkaku / h-encore / Ensō Vita. Author has not tried PS TV.
items.prerequisites: Enable unsafe homebrew for database writes; internet for browsing the theme repository.
items.data: Theme downloads selected inside the app
setup: Install imago-v1.3.0.vpk using VitaShell and enable unsafe homebrew in HENkaku Settings.
Browse psvt.ovh through Imago, install a theme, then apply it in Settings → Theme & Background → Theme.
Keep the automatic database and original-artwork backups. Local themes need a folder such as ux0:customtheme/YourTheme/theme.xml.

items.summary: Red Squirrel's established tool for online and local themes, with database backup and restore.
items.models: Author specifies HENkaku / h-encore. No exact firmware range or model matrix published.
items.prerequisites: Unsafe homebrew permission is required to install or remove themes in the system database.
items.data: Theme downloads selected inside the app
setup: Install CTManager_v4.02.vpk with VitaShell; enable unsafe homebrew and restart as the author instructs.
Create a database backup before editing themes. Browse the online repository or import an extracted local theme folder.
Apply the installed theme in Settings → Theme & Background → Theme. Version 4.02 fixes the cache/database-backup menu crash.

items.summary: An on-screen CPU, GPU, memory and FPS monitor with optional per-app clock profiles.
items.models: Stable 1.1 · author supports firmware 3.60 and 3.65 only. Newer 1.2beta is a separate pre-release.
items.prerequisites: taiHEN on supported firmware. Use one active tai config and preserve its existing entries.
setup: Copy PSVshell.skprx to ur0:tai/. In your active tai configuration, add ur0:tai/PSVshell.skprx beneath *KERNEL.
Restart the Vita. SELECT + UP or SELECT + DOWN cycles the display modes.
Leave clock settings at Default for monitoring. Manual frequencies and per-game/global profiles are optional; this page makes no measured performance claim.

items.summary: Adds a numeric battery percentage to the Vita's system status bar.
items.models: Handheld Vita. r10 source lists retail 3.55 / 3.60 / 3.65 / 3.67 / 3.68 shells; no 3.69+ claim.
items.prerequisites: taiHEN; battery display has no useful function on PS TV. Firmware identification is not a jailbreak support claim.
setup: Put shellbat.suprx in your active tai folder. This page uses ur0:tai/; the author's example uses ux0:tai/.
Add ur0:tai/shellbat.suprx beneath *main in ur0:tai/config.txt, adapting both paths consistently if your active configuration is ux0:tai/config.txt.
Restart and check the status bar. Do not infer support for newer firmware from the r10 label.

items.summary: Connect DS3, DS4 or DualSense controllers to the Vita, with up to two controllers supported.
items.models: Vita taiHEN plugin; author provides no numeric firmware range. Controller pairing limitations are documented.
items.prerequisites: A supported Bluetooth controller and taiHEN. Remove conflicting controller plugins according to the author's notes.
setup: Copy ds34vita.skprx to ur0:tai/ and add its path beneath *KERNEL in the active tai config.
If using reVita, put ds34vita after reVita. Restart and follow the author's controller-specific Bluetooth pairing procedure.
DS4 pairs with SHARE + PS and DualSense with CREATE + PS. DS3 requires its host Bluetooth address to be set by the pairing procedure; vibration is not supported.

items.summary: Remap buttons, touch and sticks, set turbo actions and save profiles for native games and Adrenaline.
items.models: Vita / PS TV on 3.60 or 3.65 only. Adrenaline menu needs a graphics filter other than Original.
items.prerequisites: taiHEN and the required ioplus.skprx below. Optional reVitaMotion.suprx adds gyro support.
setup: Copy ioplus.skprx and reVita.skprx to ur0:tai/. Add both paths beneath *KERNEL in the active tai config: ioplus first, reVita second, then ds34vita if present.
Restart. START + SQUARE opens the remapping menu; profiles and HOTKEYS.ini are stored in ux0:data/reVita/.
For optional gyro setup, copy reVitaMotion.suprx to ur0:tai/ and follow the author's SceShell/main section configuration instructions.

items.summary: A cream and black abstract theme with warped patterns and an optical illusion skull lock screen, created by Alberto Munguia.
items.models: Custom themes on a homebrew-enabled Vita. No exact firmware range or PS TV claim published by this author.
items.prerequisites: Imago or Custom Themes Manager with unsafe homebrew enabled. This ZIP contains theme assets, not an installable VPK.
setup: Create a new MINIMAL folder beneath ux0:customtheme/. Extract this ZIP into that folder; theme.xml must be directly at ux0:customtheme/MINIMAL/theme.xml. The upstream ZIP has its files at archive root.
In Imago, add the local theme folder to your Library, or use Custom Themes Manager’s local-folder install option. Keep the existing theme database backup.
Apply MINIMAL in Settings → Theme & Background → Theme. Author and version are verified from the original theme.xml.
